Class PGComms

java.lang.Object
database.PGComms
public class PGComms extends Object
Manages all application related to the PostgreSQL JDBC driver. Encapsulates all communication to the application-specific database. Manages opening and closing of connection, reads to the database and writes to the database.

PGComms is not designed to broadly work with all PostgreSQL databases, but rather specifically this application's database.

    • initialize_database

      public static void initialize_database(String server_name, String database_name, String user, String password)
      Set all required attributes of the database necessary open and close connections to it. Attributes are those of source.
      Parameters:
      server_name - The name of the server hosting the database, likely an IP or similar alias.
      database_name - The name of the database that PGComms should enable one to connect to.
      user - The name of the user PGComms will manage the database connection for.
      password - The password to the database.
      See Also:
      • source

    • test_connection

      public static boolean test_connection()
      Indicate if a successful connection was opened, then closed, to the stored database.
      Returns:
      true if the connection was opened, then closed. false if the connection could not be opened and/or closed.

    • open_connection

      private static boolean open_connection()
      Private helper function.
      Opens a connection to the database using the information stored in source. The connection is stored in conn. While the connection is open, database communication is managed using conn.
      Returns:
      true if the connection was open. false if the connection could not be opened.

    • close_connection

      private static boolean close_connection()
      Private helper function.
      Closes the connection to the database stored in conn. If conn holds null, there is no open connection, and so no connection will be closed. Once the connection is successfully closed, conn is set to null.
      Returns:
      true if the connection was closed. false if the connection could not be closed.

    • issue_query_type_update

      public static boolean issue_query_type_update(String query)
      THIS FUNCTION DOES NOT SANITIZE QUERIES!
      Issues the query specified as a parameter to the database. Queries here are "updates." These queries change data within the database. A boolean is returned which indicates the success status of the query.
      Update Queries include: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
      Parameters:
      query - The update query to be sent to the database.
      Returns:
      true if the update query was successfully processed. false if it was not.

    • are_required_nonedible_items_available

      public static boolean are_required_nonedible_items_available(int required_quantity)
      Report if all required non-edible items have an amount strictly greater than the specified amount in the inv_nonedible table.
      Required non-edible items are: Lids, Cups, Straws, Lid Covers.
      Parameters:
      required_quantity - The quantity all required non-edible items must have an inventory amount strictly greater than.
      Returns:
      true if all required non-edible inventory items have an amount above the specified quantity. Return false if this is not the case or if one of the items is not in the table.

    • get_xreport_string

      public static String get_xreport_string(String date_input)
      For each hour of the specified date, reports the total number of orders with status "completed", total number of orders voided, and total discarded. An hour that sees no orders completed, voided, nor discarded will not be reported. Times are reported assuming the time zone is America/Chicago.
      Parameters:
      date_input - The specified date, a String formatted "YYYY-MM-DD." Formatting must be followed.
      Returns:
      A string with entries separated each by two new lines. Each entry is for one hour of the day--the date and time are reported, and total number of orders completed, voided, and ordered are listed.

      If the query cannot be successfully issued, the console will print an error message.
      Parameters:
      order_id - The ID of the order to be added to orders. IDs must be unique, and the callee is expected to provide a valid, non-duplicate ID.
      status - The status of the order, which should be "completed", "void", or "discard".
      order_total - The total the order comes to, including the tip. The function ensures no floating point error occurs in adding the total to the new row.
      tip - The decimal representation of the percentage tip on the order (0.00, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, etc.).
      id_drink - The ID of the drink chosen for the order.
      id_topping1 - The ID of the first topping chosen for the order. If null, no toppings were chosen for the order.
      id_topping2 - The ID of the second topping chosen for the order. If null, no second topping was chosen for the order.
      ice_level - The amount of ice chosen for the order. 0 means "none", 1 means "light", 2 means "regular".
      sugar_level - The amount of sugar chosen for the order. 0 means 0%, 1 means 25%, 2 means 50%, 3 means 75%, 4 means 100%.
      hot_chosen - If the drink was chosen to be served hot (true) or cold (false).

    • sql_value

      private static String sql_value(String value)
      Private helper function.
      Formats/cleans a modifiable argument used in constructing a modifiable SQL statement to prevent SQL injection and incorrect interpretation of null values. A null value in java is known as null. PostgreSQL formats null values as NULL. This function will translate a null value in java to the correct, differing PostgreSQL representation. A string value in PostgreSQL can be formatted to be enclosed with ' and '. All items inside the apostrophes will be interpreted as one string. Ensures valid string values in Java are parsed as-is, and ensures these values are only read as strings by PostgreSQL. Prevents SQL injection.
      Parameters:
      value - A java value that is to be appended to a string constituting a SQL query.
      Returns:
      The "cleaned" string which will be appended to the SQL query--it can only be read as a string by PostgreSQL. If the string held null, a string with value "NULL" is returned. PostgreSQL treats NULL in queries as the null value.

    • modify_topping_quantity_in_inventory

      private static boolean modify_topping_quantity_in_inventory(int inv_id, int val, String type)
      Private helper function.
      Changes the amount of a topping in either the inv_edible or inv_nonedible tables.
      Parameters:
      inv_id - The ID (either inv_edible or inv_nonedible of the item whose quantity is to be modified.
      val - The new amount (or amount of servings) the item is to have.
      type - Specification of if the item is in inv_edible or inv_nonedible. If "inv_edible", the item is said to be in inv_edible. If "inv_nonedible", the item is said to be in inv_nonedible.
      Returns:
      true If the amount of the item was successfully changed to the specified value. false if the amount of the item was not successfully changed, or if the ID is not in either of the inventory tables.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if type is neither "inv_edible" nor "inv_nonedible".
